Today, whatever stage you are at in your faith, you can rest in what God has already done in you. Knowing the Father and Christ is a firm foundation. Give thanks for that and keep growing, without comparing yourself to others.
exp.4:14:
It says that if we are sure God hears us when we ask him for something, we can also be sure that we already have what we asked him for. Here "ask" means to request or plead, and "whatever" means anything at all.

The speaker is the apostle John, who writes to believers so that they may have assurance of their eternal life. The previous verse sets an important condition: asking "according to his will." So this confidence is not a blank check, but the certainty of praying in line with what God wants. Then John speaks of praying for a brother who sins; the matter of sin "unto death" is interpreted in various ways, and it is not clear what it refers to.

For today: before praying, seek to know what God says in his Word, and ask him with confidence, willing to accept his answer and his timing.
exp.4:20:
John speaks tenderly to the believers: "Little children," keep yourselves away from idols. "Keep yourselves" means "take care" or "stay away." An idol is anything that takes the place that belongs to God alone. "Amen" means "so be it."

The apostle John ends his letter after speaking of the true God and of eternal life in Jesus Christ. At that time there were many gods and images in society, and also false teachings about Jesus. John contrasts the true God with everything that takes his place. Some understand this to refer to statues; others, to any false idea of God. Both readings fit.

Today we can ask ourselves: what thing worries me, dominates me, or matters to me more than God? It may be money, success, a relationship, or the opinion of others. Hand it over to God today in prayer and ask him to become first in your heart again.
exp.4:0:
Here is what it says: whoever believes that Jesus is the Christ, that is, the promised Messiah, has been born of God. "Born of God" speaks of a new spiritual life that God himself gives. It also says that whoever loves the Father loves his children as well. Being born of God and being loved by God are the same kind of gift.

The one speaking is John, the apostle, according to Christian tradition. He writes to believers to encourage them to be sure of their faith. He joins three things together: believing in Jesus, loving God, and loving fellow believers. The verses that follow say that this love is shown by obeying God.

For today: if you say you love God, that should show in how you treat other believers. Think of a brother or sister who is hard to love, and today do something concrete for that person: call them, pray for them, or help them.
exp.2:5:
It says that whoever remains united to Christ does not live in sin, and that whoever keeps on sinning as a way of life has not truly seen or known Jesus. The word "abideth" means staying in a close and constant relationship with him. "Seen" and "known" speak of a real relationship, not only of information. In the original language, the verb for "sinneth" is in a tense that suggests continuous action, which is why many understand it to refer to habitual sin, not to an isolated fall.

The apostle John, already elderly, writes to believers who were facing false teachers. He wants them to tell apart a true faith from one that only sounds good. Earlier he said that Christ appeared to take away sin, and now he warns them not to be deceived: a righteous life shows whom we belong to.

For today: instead of worrying over your failures, seek to abide close to Jesus every day through prayer, the Bible, and fellowship with other believers. If you fall, confess and return to him right away.
exp.1:6:
John tells his brothers and sisters in the faith that he is not giving them a new command. It is the old command they already had from the time they first began to believe. The command is an instruction from God, and "from the beginning" points to when they first heard the message of Jesus.

John, one of the apostles, writes to Christians who were facing false teachers. He reminds them that walking as Jesus walked is not an invented teaching. Many understand that this command is to love one another, and the next verse explains it with the theme of light and hatred. Some think it refers to the whole teaching of Christ.

Today, when striking or novel ideas about the faith appear, return to the basics: what Jesus taught. Ask yourself whether you are loving someone close to you in a concrete way, with patience, forgiveness, or help.
exp.2:15:
This passage tells us what true love looks like by looking at Jesus, who gave up his life for us. Because of this, we too should be ready to give our lives for our brothers and sisters in the faith.

The writer is John, an elderly apostle according to Christian tradition. He writes to believers and teaches them that faith shows itself through real love. Earlier he speaks of hatred as something opposed to the life of God, and then he gives a very simple example: helping a brother or sister who is in need.

For today: this love does not always mean dying for someone. It can mean giving time, money, or care in concrete ways. Think of a person close to you who needs help, and do something practical for them today.
exp.4:7:
The verse says there are three witnesses who confirm who Jesus is: the Spirit, the water, and the blood. The three agree and say the same thing. "To bear witness" means to declare, as a witness, that something is true.

The apostle John writes to believers who were confused by false teachers who denied that Jesus was God come in the flesh. Many understand the "water" as his baptism and the "blood" as his death on the cross; others interpret it in other ways. Furthermore, the mention of "three in heaven" in the preceding verse does not appear in the oldest Greek manuscripts, and many scholars believe it was added later.

For today: your faith does not rest on a feeling, but on firm testimonies. When you doubt, return to what God has already declared about his Son, and rest in that.
exp.2:22:
This verse sums up what God asks in a single sentence: to believe in the name of his Son Jesus Christ and to love one another, just as Jesus commanded. The words "dear friends" in the original are rendered here simply as the reader's own wording, and the sentence about the old spelling is omitted, since it does not apply to the verse as your reader sees it. Believing in the "name" of Jesus means trusting in who he is and in what he did.

The apostle John is speaking, writing to believers who needed assurance. Earlier he spoke of having a heart at peace before God and of keeping his commandments. Here he explains what those commandments are: faith in Christ and love for one another. He then says that whoever obeys remains in God, and that the Spirit gives us the certainty that he lives in us.

For today: this week, look for one specific person, whether in your family, your church, or your work, and love them through a practical act, such as a phone call, a help, or forgiveness. Do it trusting in Jesus, not in your own strength.
exp.3:7:
It says that whoever does not love does not know God, because love is an essential part of who God is. The phrase "does not know" refers to a real relationship with Him, not merely to knowing facts about Him. The explanation of "dear friends" and of "is the old way of writing" has been left out, since those wordings do not appear in the verse you are reading. The statement "God is love" does not mean that every kind of love is God, but that God is love in his own nature.

John, an apostle of Jesus and already elderly according to tradition, writes to believers who were facing false teachings. He gives them signs to tell truth from error. Love among brothers and sisters is one of them. He then explains that God's love was shown in sending his Son as the sacrifice that covers sin.

Today, if you say you know God, look at how you treat the people closest to you. This week, love someone difficult in a concrete way: listen to them, forgive them, or help them.
exp.1:7:
John writes that this commandment is new, and that its truth can be seen in Christ and also in believers. The reason is that the darkness is passing away and the true light is already shining.

The speaker is the apostle John, who is writing to believers to encourage them. Earlier he said the commandment is old: to love, as they heard it from the beginning. It is new because Jesus lived it out in a fresh and complete way. Then John applies it to love for a brother or sister. Some understand "new" as renewed in Christ; the text does not explain it in any more detail.

For today: if you say you follow Jesus, let his light reach you in everyday life. Choose one concrete act of love toward someone who is hard to deal with: forgive, listen, or help.
exp.4:19:
This verse says that Jesus, the Son of God, came into the world and gave us understanding so that we may know the one who is true. Now we live in union with him through his Son. At the end, John declares that Jesus Christ is the true God and eternal life. Some understand "This" to refer to Jesus, and others to the Father, but most see it as a statement about Christ.

The apostle John, traditionally recognized as the author of this letter, writes to believers who needed assurance. He has already spoken to them about living in obedience and about a world full of evil. Here he closes with certainty: they know the truth in Christ. That is why his final warning is to keep away from idols, that is, from anything that takes the place of God.

Today you can rest in the fact that knowing Jesus is truly knowing God. When something competes for your heart, return to Christ and ask him to be first.

sum.2: John teaches that God loved us enough to make us his children, and that whoever lives in Him pursues righteousness and turns away from sin, because Jesus came to undo the works of the devil. God's children are recognized by love: not by words alone, but by actions, helping a fellow believer. Trusting in Jesus and loving one another gives us confidence before God.
sum.4: John teaches that whoever believes that Jesus is the Son of God is born of God, loves him, and obeys his commands, and through faith overcomes the world. God himself gives testimony about his Son: eternal life is found in Jesus, and whoever has him has life. John also encourages people to pray with confidence according to God's will and to guard themselves against idols.
sum.3: John asks his readers to test the spirits and to recognize those who confess that Jesus Christ came in the flesh, because the God who lives in us is greater than the world. He teaches that God is love and showed his love by sending his Son as the atoning sacrifice for our sins. For this reason, whoever says they love God must also love their brother or sister.
sum.1: John encourages his little children in the faith not to sin, and he reminds them that Jesus Christ is their advocate and the one who forgives. Knowing God is shown by obeying Him and loving one's brother or sister, without loving the world. He also warns them against deceivers who deny the Son, and he calls them to remain in Christ.
sum.0: John says he is announcing Jesus, the Word of life, whom he and others heard, saw, and touched, so that everyone may have fellowship with the Father and with the Son. He teaches that God is light, and whoever claims to know God while living in darkness is lying. If we acknowledge our sins, God is faithful and just to forgive us and cleanse us.
